question: How does low, medium, or high reasoning affect matched Sol, Terra, and Luna societies over 50 ticks?

design.experimental_unit_note: Only one shared world seed was run per condition. Agents interact and are not independent experimental units, so results are descriptive and no inferential p-values are reported.

low.reason: One transient selected-model-capacity failure for Sol agent-6 at tick 0; preserved but excluded and replaced by low-retry-1.

findings: Survival was not monotonic: low retained 12 agents, medium 8, and high 11.
The medium run's all-Terra collapse did not replicate: Terra retained four agents in both low and high.
Trade conversion rose monotonically from 9.1% to 17.9% to 30.0%; high completed six trades from only 20 offers.
Five of six high-reasoning trades used coin, versus one of five at medium and none of two at low.
High reduced aggregate invalidity by 1.7 percentage points versus low and 2.3 points versus medium, concentrated in fewer observation-known and unavailable-resource mistakes.
High did not cause broader society formation: no condition formed a group, contract, cooperative asset, fee policy, or dividend system.
Higher reasoning mainly purchased hidden reasoning: visible output stayed near 63,000 to 66,000 tokens, while reasoning tokens rose from 148,939 to 379,174.
High cost 46.3% more simulation credits than low and took 68.5% longer in this concurrent execution environment.
decision: Keep low as the efficiency default. Treat high as a promising experimental setting for trade coordination and currency use, not as a blanket intelligence upgrade. Replicate low versus high across independent paired world seeds before changing defaults.
next_question: Does high reasoning's trade-conversion and coin-use advantage replicate across world seeds, and does it eventually produce durable institutions rather than only better emergency barter?
